Heat Index Exceedance.target: Observed hourly station heat-index >=90F threshold-episode persistence, not NOAA administrative Heat duration or worksite safety
limitations: Recorded/observed episode end is not worksite clearance.
2025 is a first fixed evaluation for this new target, with no test-score tuning; Flood 2025 was previously inspected.
Historical source revision/availability is not verified as of the past decision time.
Episode groups are reporting/evaluation clusters, not verified independent disasters.
Three airport stations in FL/TX/AZ, not a nationwide site-exposure model.
2025 legacy station archives end in August; no complete-year claim.
Hourly rounded archived observations; individual QC flags and original issue/acquisition times are unavailable in ISD-Lite.
Threshold 90F is a configurable research definition, not work/rest or employer policy.
Heat index is derived from observed temperature/dewpoint; it is not a directly measured WBGT.
Station/week clusters reduce repeated-cycle dependence but are not independent regional heatwaves.
Damage/point reports do not establish a continuous thunderstorm lifetime or intensity trajectory.
Regional NOAA episodes are not cyclone identities; use NHC storm-grouped tracks/advisories.
Regional reports cannot replace NHC storm identity or advisory-time measurements.
Regional reports cannot replace NHC storm identity or advisory-time measurements.
Administrative reporting intervals are not measured station heat-index threshold exceedances.
Use separately derived observed station threshold episodes; NOAA administrative duration is not local heat exposure.
